findings.problem: LeaseWorkflow has no explicit state machine; any combination of status string, is_validated bool, and is_sent bool is representable including logically impossible ones like status='sent' with is_sent=false
findings.failure_mode: invalid state combinations silently persist; callers cannot rely on any invariant and must manually cross-check all fields every time
findings.fix: replace status, is_validated, is_sent with a single LeaseState enum with variants like New, Validated, Sent, each variant carrying only the data it owns

findings.problem: status is pub status: String allowing any string value including typos, invalid transitions, and non-deterministic equality checks
findings.failure_mode: a caller can set status to "sentt" or "pending" when the lease is already sent, creating silent domain violations with no compile-time guard
findings.fix: replace with pub status: LeaseStatus enum using exhaustive match at every call site

findings.problem: is_validated and is_sent are independent booleans that encode lifecycle state but can contradict each other (e.g. is_validated=false, is_sent=true means an unvalidated lease was sent)
findings.failure_mode: business invariant 'leases must be validated before sent' is invisible to the type system; invalid workflows compile and run silently
findings.fix: collapse into a single typestate enum: LeaseState::New, LeaseState::Validated, LeaseState::Sent

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is detached from the boolean is_sent flag; a lease can have is_sent=true with None timestamp (lost data) or is_sent=false with Some timestamp (ghost data)
findings.failure_mode: timestamp is stored independently of lifecycle state, so the invariant 'sent leases always have a timestamp' must be checked manually at every access point
findings.fix: move timestamp into the enum variant: LeaseState::Sent { sent_at: Instant } or LeaseState::Sent(u64)

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive domain identifier with no constraints; it is interchangeable with any other String field including status
findings.failure_mode: accidental swapping of id and status values is a compile-time impossibility to catch; callers must manually validate id format at every usage
findings.fix: replace with pub id: LeaseId where LeaseId is a newtype wrapping a validated String or String with a smart constructor

findings.problem: raw primitives String cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors; LeaseWorkflow fields are all pub and accept any value, so callers can construct invalid domain states directly
findings.failure_mode: no constructor enforces invariants at the boundary; any caller can create a LeaseWorkflow with contradictory fields and bypass all domain rules
findings.fix: make all fields private, provide a fallible LeaseWorkflow::try_new or builder with invariant checks, and use smart constructors at the shell boundary

findings.problem: mark_sent blindly sets status='sent' and is_sent=true regardless of whether the lease was validated; is_validated is never checked
findings.failure_mode: unvalidated leases can be sent without any guard, violating the business invariant that validation must precede sending
findings.fix: remove mark_sent from the struct; use an enum-based state machine where Sent is only reachable via a Validated->Sent transition enforced at compile time

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent or any hot-path measurement

no allocation evidence for String-based status (heap allocation per instance)
no second-ring evidence: no clippy run, no cargo check, no test execution

residual_risk: static code review only; no commands were run. The struct is a trivial 13-line file with no hidden complexity, so runtime evidence would not change the findings. The typestate violations are structural and would be confirmed by inspection rather than execution.
